newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy unions mixed over mini-budget proposals.
newsitem.headline: Italy unions mixed over mini-budget proposals.

text.p: Leaders of Italy's three main unions criticised one measure in the government's planned corrective mini-budget on Wednesday while giving a nod to the rest of the package.
CISL leader Sergio D'Antoni said the three objected to government plans to hold back end-of-contract retirement settlements to state workers for six months.
"We expressed a strong objection," he said after the leaders met centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi, whose cabinet is expected to approve the package on Thursday.
CGIl leader Sergio Cofferati said however that the unions were not going to pass any full judgement on the mini-budget until it had been finalised and approved.
"We will do so only when the government announces its decisions. For the moment we can appreciate that which has not been done," he told reporters.
"In relation to recent leaks, it seems to me a mini-budget of, fortunately, a fairer character than predicted.
"On the subject of the state settlements we indicated several alternatives that we hope the government will take into consideration tomorrow," Cofferati added.
All three union leaders deemed the rest of the package to be useful in helping the government's aim of keeping Italy on track for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"They are measures that help take a step towards Europe," declared Cofferati.
The package will include around 16 trillion lire ($9.5 billion) of deficit-cutting measures.
They include obliging firms to pay taxes on huge severance payment funds two years ahead of time.
